newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SPANISH FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND MATCHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPANISH FIRST DIVISION WEEKEND MATCHES.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this weekend in the Spanish first division (kick-off times 1500 GMT unless stated, league positions in brackets):
Betis won at Tenerife in the 1994-95 season and again last year with two goals in the last five minutes but have shown signs of weakness in their bid for second place in recent games.

Valladolid surprised then champions-elect Atletico in last season's fixture and will be boosted ahead of this clash for UEFA Cup places by Wednesday's victory over Barcelona and the absence of injured Atletico midfielder Jose Luis Caminero.

Sporting fired coach Benito Floro after slipping into the relegation zone with Wednesday's 4-0 defeat at Athletic Bilbao. New boss Miguel Montes is set to bring in striker Hugo Perez against an Extremadura side missing key forward Silvani.
Sevilla need to haul in a ten-point gap to avoid automatic relegation, and are still suffering after letting Real Madrid turn a 2-0 Sevilla lead into a 4-2 defeat on Wednesday.
Logrones have clocked up six successive defeats and desperately need a result against a Deportivo side that have dropped only five of the last 27 points under new coach Carlos Alberto Silva.

Compostela are unbeaten at home in six games, but are still not clear of a danger area that includes over half the teams in the first division. Hercules are still six points adrift of avoiding one of the four slots leading to automatic relegation.

Rayo have never won at Zaragoza, who were boosted in their bid to avoid relegation by the midweek draw at high-flying Real Betis. The home side will be without suspended defenders Javier Aguado and Garcia Sarjuan.
Real have gone nine games without victory while Oviedo are managerless after firing Juan Manuel Lillo after Thursday's disastrous 5-1 home defeat by Racing Santander.

Espanyol hung on for a goalless draw against Atletico on Thursday but will be without suspended defender Mauricio Pocchetino against Racing, who took their 300th league victory in fine style on Thursday by thrashing Oviedo 5-1.

Barcelona are now ten points adrift of leaders Real, but hope to keep up the pressure in their bid for Spain's second European Cup place against an Athletic side that is looking good for a UEFA Cup berth.
Real's biggest danger will be over-confidence after coming back to beat Sevilla 4-2 in midweek. It is a problem UEFA Cup hopefuls Valencia will look to exploit.
